review: Обожаю когда в играх прорабатывают мелочи. Больше это касается не геймплея или визуала, хотя он и передаёт эту гнетущую атмосферу холодного космоса, в котором мы брошены на гигантском корабле среди разных тварей и сломанных механизмов, а сюжетной составляющей. Если уж собрались проходить стазис, то читайте записки (как минимум потому что в некоторых моментах они нужны для решения головоломок). Можно конечно просто пробежаться по сюжету и забыть его, но записки настолько круто его дополняют и становятся интереснее основной игры. Благодаря им корабль ощущается настолько же живым, насколько и мёртвым, например, локация где ты читаешь о любовном треугольнике членов экипажа над их изуродованными до неузнаваемости телами: один парень, готовый ради девушки отдать всё и даже жизнь; девушка, которая понимает что человек испытывает к ней чувства и специально уделяет внимания другому; и второй парень влюбленный в первого и вынужденный скрывать свои чувства, единственное его утешение это кот, за которым и так тяжело присматривать в пучинах космоса... Вы скажите это херня? Но когда ты читаешь о переживаниях гея, то сначала тебе забавно, ну вспомнив что ты читаешь над кровавым месивом, а чуть позже встречаешь кота, которого он потерял и много времени уделил на поиски (при том что на судне уже начались беспорядки), и на твоих глазах его разрывает чудище, то становится не так смешно. В общем, советую для прохождения если любите погружаться в лор с головой

I'm covered in bees!!! If you get it, you get it.

Seriously though, the game is janky as hell but kind of charming. Like a good low budget horror, which is basically what this is in point and click form. The puzzle solutions are often mental combinations of items like severed limbs and intestines to open a door (like why? The whole ship is basically made out of loose wires...) or filling gloves with acid... basically solutions that would only make sense to a dev who is up at 4am surrounded by empty cans of energy drink in a state of sleep deprived delirium. So you end up sort of brute-forcing your way through the puzzles because they are largely an exercise in trial and error and can sometimes result in hilariously grotesque deaths. Some of the deaths are essentially unavoidable because the most obvious solution to a rational person is fatal. I guess it's the devs having fun with it which is part of the charm though.

But despite the jankiness and insanity, the atmosphere is great and I couldn't stop playing. They knew what they wanted to make but just did it a bit amateurishly.

[h1]ИЗОМЕТРИЧЕСКИЙ DEAD SPACE[/h1]

Из минусов: сохранения идут не в Стим кеш, а напрямую на компьютер. Поэтому если появится необходимость продолжить прохождение на другом устройстве - придётся копировать сейвы на флешку и вручную перемещать на носитель.

[h1]SANGRE, DOLOR Y LÁGRIMAS EN EL ESPACIO PROFUNDO[/h1]

Aventura isométrica de terror, desarrollada con muy pocos medios por un pequeño estudio independiente, 
pero que consigue ser muy eficaz, contundente y entretenida.

Despertamos de un sueño criogénico a bordo de una nave científica en el espacio profundo y solo sabemos que junto a nuestra mujer e hija, en paradero desconocido, hemos sido secuestrados y desconocemos por quién ni por qué. Solo sabemos que tenemos que buscar a nuestra desaparecida familia y de paso encontrar las respuestas a todo lo que esta sucediendo a nuestro alrededor. 

Y con esta premisa nos embarcamos de lleno en esta aventura gráfica de terror donde pronto vamos descubriendo que algo realmente terrible le ha pasado a la nave y su tripulación. Testigos a la fuerza del profundo horror que se ha apoderado de todo lo que nos rodea mientras intentamos no sucumbir a la desesperación.

Visualmente resulta de lo más atractivo con su cuidada y pulida perspectiva isométrica, y si bien es cierto que el manejo y el movimiento del personaje, así como la propia interface del juego, se siente algo toscos y limitados el resultado final se equilibra y se compensa con una elaborada carga narrativa que no tiene complejo alguno y que se atreve a abordar temas profundamente oscuros y perturbadores. 

[i]STASIS[/i] es ante todo una aventura de terror que se hace notar en todo momento gracias a su profunda narrativa, que en líneas generales se puede decir que abusa de las notas encontradas en los terminales de los tripulantes pero es que las limitaciones técnicas son las que son, y también a no cortarse en más mínimo a la hora de presentar en pantalla los sucesos más escabrosos y truculentos. 

Y es que sin duda estamos ante un juego pensado y desarrollado para adultos, no solo por los temas que trata sino por como decide abordarlos y presentárselos al jugador. De hecho, la idea de dela depresión y la desesperación sobre vuela constantemente sobre el título y no es casualidad que en un descarado ejercicio de humor negro la mayoría de los logros que otorga el juego se concedan por las múltiples y diferentes formas que tiene nuestro protagonista de quitarse la vida y acabar de una vez con todo el horror y la desesperación que le rodea. 

La dificultad, salvo en algún puzle no muy bien explicado, es más bien limitada porque siempre vamos a encontrar la solución muy cerca de donde se van desarrollando los acontecimientos y el juego no está concebido para poner a prueba tu tolerancia a los retos y a quedarte atascado a cada pocos pasos sino para contarte una historia sólida y bien elaborada, que es donde reside su mayor acierto. 

Artísticamente el juego cumple con creces, con un diseño gráfico limitado pero visualmente atractivo y unos efectos sonoros que siempre están presentes y colaboran enormemente a que la atmosfera de horror y tensión nunca nos abandonen.

[h1]Conclusiones de un secuestrado padre de familia que despierta por sorpresa en el espacio profundo[/h1]

[i]STASIS[/i] es una interesante y terrorífica aventura que, pese a sus limitaciones técnicas y abuso de las notas encontradas, merece realmente la pena y no para de mejorar según nos vamos acercando a su desenlace final. 

Sus más que posibles defectos se ven ampliamente compensados por una trama adulta y desgarradora, valiente a la hora de cruzar ciertos limites que otros juegos no se atreven a cruzar, y también por una más que lograda ambientación de terror espacial. 

Se le podría echar en cara una mayor "finura" a la hora de presentar los puzles y algunos de los elementos propios de las aventuras gráficas pero según uno va avanzando en el juego pronto se da cuenta de que estos no son más que un medio para un fin, el narrativo, bien distinto. 

RECOMENDABLE para todo aventurero que se precie, sobre todo por los amantes del terror que saben por experiencia propia que sus gritos, en el espacio profundo, nunca serán escuchados. 

ESCAPAR COMO SI NO HUBIERA UN MAÑANA los intolerantes a la lectura, los ofendiditos con las situaciones políticamente incorrectas y los cobardes que se asustan de su propia sombra.

I had never played a point & click game before, so it was a wild ride for me. I'm gonna point out ONE defect this game has, and that's its "logic". Stasis is basically a game-long puzzle where you need to figure out which item to use where. Sometimes these puzzles make sense, but sometimes they absolutely don't. In order not to spoil anything, I'm gonna give an example with everyday situations. It's stuff like "let's smash these strawberries with the heel of a boot so we can make alcohol", or "let me touch this wall so that I can pick up the chair next to it, even though I saw the chair first", or even "remember how I told you that there's absolutely no way you can go through walls? Well now you can, but I'm not gonna tell you that".
I had to look up solutions at least 5 times during my playthrough because I was stuck for about 20 minutes in each of these times. And it always turned out to be something that made me say "really?"
Despite that, I enjoyed my time with the game. It has a deep lore, interesting characters and a lot (A LOT) of text to read. It is good at building up tension and fear, but lacks in making that fear come true. Even then, I'd say it's worth it for the price.

复古科幻恐怖，等距视角，点击推动式解谜......如此完美符合我的调性的tag。在发现这个游戏的瞬间，我震惊了，这样一部神作，为什么我从来没有听说过？
好吧......它没有被评为神作的原因很快就暴露出来了。抛开精致的美术之后，在游玩过程中，这个游戏的缺点逐渐暴露了出来：这游戏的很多地方明显是为了猎奇而猎奇的。这并不一定成为一个缺点，但在stasis里它确确实实地拖垮了游戏，因为为了猎奇而猎奇这一点做得太露骨了。为了猎奇，包含剧情合理性、情感体验在内的不少方面都被牺牲掉了，让这游戏更像是一部高经费的互动式cult片而不是成功的点击解谜。
比如，这游戏里的很多解谜道具可以被主角用来自杀，steam成就里也有一半是为各种猎奇自杀方式准备的，但是根据剧情主角在这里这么果断地自杀根本就解释不通。动画也很不合理，比如轻松地一只手把台球杆插进自己身体，像是拿竹签戳章鱼烧一样。
再比如，太多被突然抬出的概念没有得到合理的解释说明。地图上一些让人震撼的生物，机器，和死者的猎奇死状，还有导致了大量猎奇场景出现的“某某计划”，“某某项目”，本来我以为会有个合理的剧情解释，结果直到结局都没有填坑，好像就是为了制造猎奇场景而临时抬出的概念。即使把PDA里的内容全部读完也一样。
在以上问题的拖累之下，游戏的剧情变得相当平淡。优秀的美术和情感丰沛的配音确实给游戏增色不少，但是拿开它们再看剧情，简直没有一丝闪光点，只有折磨主角和对这一行为的不成功的合理化尝试。其它部分也大抵如此，比如解谜道具拾取没有剧情锁导致主角做出在当时的玩家看来很意义不明的事情（比如毫无理由地去拿一堆尸块），背离逻辑的道具用法（比如拿手枪当研磨杵用），有瑕疵的人物动画（穿墙、瞬移、来回走）......
好在stasis的美术实在太顶了，难有替代，导致整体玩下来的体验不至于连一个好评也值不上。如果是希望得到优秀的剧情体验，我可以说这个游戏不适合你；但是如果你不太在意剧情，这个游戏是值得一玩的。

Because i know i'm in for a long time sitting there reading, trying to soak everything up so I don't miss content... In both games I just started skimming them, and outright ignoring many as I went along. 
What I would LIKE to see, is maybe a vocal recording instead of text? So that we could pick up a PDA and have it read to us as we are exploring the area. That way momentum wouldnt stop, and it would still fit the overall vibe of the games very well, still.  If something like that was implemented, these would be near perfect, imo.

Oh, and some of the puzzles/solutions... Holy hell, random as F. I mean, some puzzles are the "just try clicking on everything to find the solution" style. Which I dislike. And I swear some of those solutions are just so damn random that I can't imagine anyone would think "oh of course I just combine _____ and ________, or "obviously I just put ______ on the table and smack it with _________, it's so clear!"

Плохо, но не настолько всё печально, как с прямым сиквелом игры. По сути, единственный элемент, который лично меня смог зацепить - арт-дизайн локаций. Местные локации в вайбе "Ишимуры дома" с трупами, кровищей, темнотой и разрухой вполне себе доставляют. И ощущения от общего вайба локаций усиливает звук, который здесь очень и очень хорош. Главный герой не стесняется орать, плакать, истерически смеяться, чавкать, как мукбангер, что в местную атмосферу укладывается. 
Но вот сам главный герой, семья, которую он ищет и которую нам покажут два раза за всю игру, антагонист, который становится шизоучёным за одну строчку записки- это то, что персонально во мне пробуждает огромную скуку, ибо пустой главный герой хоть и ходит по симпотным локациям, издавая разные стремные звуки, но ни его характер, ни его путь в игре вообще не представлены. Семья главного героя, антагонист- туда же, просто картонки, которые на экране что-то делают. Напарница главного героя чуть получше, но это отрыв в пару процентов, не больше. 
Эта игра, конечно, не про вселенский масштаб бедствий, но ощущается все как задел на что-то глобальное, на что-то крупное. Но ощущение это как возникло у меня, так и пропало, ибо масштаб этот за пределы мыслей людей в записках никуда и не вышел. 
Самих же записок в игре очень много, но интересных очень мало, потому что многое в них попытались запихнуть: зачатки взаимоотношений между персонажами, которые часто никуда не ведут, характеры авторов этих записок, которые тоже не всегда приводят к тому, что описывается в этих записках, разные события после местного дня Х - наброски, которые должны расширять местный лор (и которые его расширяют отчасти), но которые наполнены таким количеством лишней херни, что читать их в один момент становится дико скучно.
Сюжета здесь также лучше не ждать: проснулся -> найди способ сбежать с корабля и семью по пути найти не забудь. 
Ну и концовка, которая, вроде, должна показать жестокую иронию ситуации, в которую попал главный герой, но эта ирония случается с картонками на экране. 
Не могу однозначно сказать *играть в это не стоит*, но многого ждать не стоит, т.к., на мой взгляд, игра банально слишком слабенькая, из-за чего многие стандартные запросы отработать не может.

A Short but Unforgettable Sci-Fi Horror Experience

Stasis is one of the best horror games I’ve played in a long time. While it's on the shorter side, it delivers a gripping and intense experience from start to finish. The atmosphere is nearly perfect — the visuals, sound design, and especially the music create a deeply immersive environment that had me on edge the entire time. My heart was pounding more than once as I made my way through its eerie corridors and chilling story.

The narrative really stands out. It doesn’t just ask you to reflect on moral dilemmas — it forces you to consider the justifications behind the scientists’ actions, which adds a fascinating and disturbing layer to the experience. It’s not just a horror game; it’s a psychological one too.

Puzzles are plentiful and well-designed, giving your brain something to chew on while the tension builds around you. The game had me fully invested until the very end.

My only real complaint is that I couldn’t manually adjust the volume. It was louder than I would’ve liked, and having no control over that was a bit frustrating — just a personal pet peeve. That said, the sound design does contribute well to the overall tension and tone of the game.

For the current price, Stasis is absolutely worth it. I highly recommend it to fans of sci-fi horror, especially those who appreciate a strong story and atmosphere. I can’t wait to dive into the next installment.

Але щойно занурюєшся у світ гри, зовнішні недоліки перестають мати значення.

Головна сила Stasis — це дивовижно огидна і водночас захоплива атмосфера. Темні коридори, бридкі деталі довколишнього середовища, моторошні звукові ефекти — усе це створює відчуття глибокого дискомфорту й напруження, якого рідко досягають навіть великі хорор-проєкти. I finally got around to playing Stasis, an isometric point-and-click adventure game that caught my interest the moment I saw the screenshots and tried the free prequel, Cayne, back in 2017 (according to my Steam logs). After sitting in my backlog for years due to other priorities, both in life and gaming, I eventually dived in this year on my Steam Deck. Like most point-and-click adventure games, it proved ideal for handheld play, with the interface working flawlessly and no awkward remapping required.

Stasis was originally released in 2015 by The Brotherhood, a small South African studio founded by two brothers, Chris and Nic Bischoff. Chris handled much of the art and design, and the project was funded via Kickstarter, taking roughly five years to develop. Their aim was to blend old-school adventure mechanics with the tense atmosphere of modern sci-fi horror films, drawing heavily from classics such as Alien and Event Horizon. The game also features a soundtrack by Mark Morgan, known for his work on Fallout and Planescape: Torment, which alone hints at the mood they were aiming for. Stasis eventually expanded into a series, with the free prequel, Cayne, that I mentioned, and a full sequel, Stasis: Bone Totem, both of which further explore its universe and themes.

The game places you in the role of John Maracheck, an ordinary man who wakes up disoriented and in pain aboard the massive, derelict spaceship Groomlake, which orbits above Neptune. John had been travelling with his wife Ellen and daughter Rebecca, all in stasis for what was supposed to be a routine corporate transport run, but he emerges alone and confused. The Groomlake is a dark maze of blood-streaked hallways, ruined laboratories, malfunctioning machinery, and shadows broken by emergency lighting. As John, you explore the ship, scavenging clues from PDAs, computer terminals, and environmental details that gradually reveal the nature of the experiments conducted there under the Cayne Corporation. Rather than relying on jump scares, the story  favours slow-burn tension, where the horror comes from discovery and from confronting what is already known rather than what lurks around the corner, whilst still including occasional twists. Along the way, you interact with a few key characters; John himself is an everyman caught in terrifying circumstances, motivated primarily by the hope of finding his family alive, whereas, Te’ah, a scientist who contacts John via radio, offers guidance whilst keeping her motives ambiguous enough to create tension. The shadow of Dr. Malan, the main antagonist, also hangs over everything. His logs reveal his gradual descent into madness, painting him as a researcher warped by ambition and isolation. Frankly, at times, the game feels like a hybrid between Dead Space, with its isolated ship horror and body horror, and Sanitarium, with its psychological unraveling and sometimes dreamlike sequences. As previously mentioned, it also clearly takes inspiration from films such as Alien, though unlike Alien, there is no stalking creature chasing you through the corridors. True, for players who are very picky about originality, this reliance on familiar source material might make parts of the game feel derivative, but ultimately, the execution is compelling enough to keep you engaged.

The game’s strengths show the passion behind this small-team project. The atmosphere is thick and oppressive. The isometric visuals are finely detailed, with every corridor and lab rendered in a way that feels both lived-in and decayed. Flickering lights cast distorted shadows, rusted metal drips with fluids, and rooms filled with the remnants of grotesque experiments are unsettling to explore. Sound design reinforces this, with distant clangs echoing like footsteps, whispers carried through vents, and the hum of failing machinery making the ship itself feel hostile. The puzzles mostly integrate well with the environment. Many involve using items in unsettling ways, such as repurposing medical tools for grim problem solving or rerouting broken circuits to progress. Optional crew logs and PDAs add depth, humanising the tragedy by showing how ordinary lives were warped by corporate negligence. Furthermore, the voice acting for John and Te’ah is solid, with John’s pain and desperation coming through in subtle details, and Te’ah’s voice hinting at her own trauma. Additionally, Mark Morgan’s score gives everything a cinematic edge, combining ambient drones with bursts of tension that kept me engaged.

That said, Stasis is far from flawless. Some puzzles can be frustratingly unintuitive, a classic point-and-click curse, requiring peculiar item combinations that feel unnatural. At times, progress can rely more on blind trial and error than clever deduction. The lack of a hotspot highlight makes pixel hunting in dark areas an occasional issue, which can also sometimes prove particularly tiresome on the smaller Steam Deck screen compared to a PC monitor. The writing also falters slightly with Dr. Malan, who leans too heavily into the archetype of a ranting mad scientist, spouting lines about “playing God” that clash with the otherwise grounded tone of the story. Furthermore, the game’s structure is more linear than I anticipated and can demand a fair amount of backtracking across the Groomlake’s decks. This becomes monotonous when combined with some trial-and-error puzzle solving, as you might check one room, then a floor above, then another, only to be wrong repeatedly. Without fast travel or some clearer objective markers, tense exploration can sometimes slip into repetitive wandering.

There are also aspects that sit somewhere in the middle. As previously alluded, the game involves reading, with PDAs and computer terminals filled with logs, crew profiles, and corporate memos. I personally enjoyed diving into them, as they fleshed out the world, but I can see how they might overwhelm players who just want to push forward. The gore is extremely graphic at times, full of mutilations, body horror, and failed augmentations. It fits the theme and story, but will undoubtedly put off anyone sensitive to that kind of imagery. There is also a touch of dark humour, such as Steam achievements that reward you for dying in gruesome ways, for example venting yourself into space or tampering with unstable machinery that kills you. Moreover, the game is fairly short, around six to ten hours depending on how much time you spend reading optional logs or exploring. That length works well, keeping the pace tight, though it left me wishing for more side stories or branching paths given the richness of the setting. The pre-rendered backgrounds are mostly static compared to fully dynamic environments in modern games, but I found the retro style charming and fitting for the isometric perspective.

In conclusion, I genuinely enjoyed Stasis despite some flaws and its heavy reliance on familiar inspirations. It is a moody, atmospheric horror point-and-click adventure in an isometric perspective that fully immerses you in its world. The detailed visuals, haunting sound design, and strong narrative hooks make it feel far larger than its indie budget suggests. Some puzzles can be frustrating, backtracking repetitive at times, and perhaps one or two characters slightly underdeveloped for my liking, but the strengths clearly outweigh the weaknesses. The game builds its horror through discovery and atmosphere rather than cheap scares, leaving a lasting impression in my opinion. Sure, the pixel hunting at times can be a minor nuisance in darker areas, but even on the Steam Deck, the experience remains smooth and engaging. I am now looking forward to try out the sequel, Bone Totem, at some point, as of writing this. Stasis is well worth playing, alongside the free prequel, Cayne, for additional story context, even if not essential. Comes recommended for anyone seeking an impactful (sci-fi horror) point-and-click adventure game.
